# Allowed XLSForm Syntax

## Row types are an allowlist

error — the registry is an allowlist; any survey-sheet type that is neither registered nor a metadata row MUST abort the transformation with a clear message

Metadata rows (`start`, `end`, `today`, `deviceid`, `username`, `audit`) are accepted and carried but produce no authored question. Every other `type` must be one of the registered question / structural types.

## Names & choice codes

Write names and choice codes as letters and digits only (`^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$`), e.g. `jobsatisfaction` or `jobSatisfaction`: no underscores, hyphens, spaces or umlauts. The only exception is the `<question>_other` companion row. The validator rejects anything else. `FieldSanitizer` produces conforming names from free text: it transliterates (`ä`→`ae`, `ß`→`ss`), drops other diacritics, deletes the remaining non-alphanumerics and truncates, so keep the stem short and unambiguous:

- **Variable `name`:** ≤ 20 chars after stripping. Must be unique — duplicates get a numeric suffix.
- **Choice `name` (code):** ≤ 5 chars after stripping — longer codes are truncated in LimeSurvey, so short codes (or plain integers, as in the examples) are safest.
- Labels/hints carry the human text; keep names/codes machine-stable.

## Choices sheet

`select_one` / `select_multiple` rows reference a `list_name`. Define options on the `choices` sheet with columns `list_name`, `name` (code), `label`. Every `list_name` used on the survey sheet must exist on the choices sheet.

## `or_other` pattern (open “Other” field)

Applies to: `select_one`, `select_multiple`. Add a choice with code `other`, then a companion row of type `text` named `<question>_other` directly after the question, shown only when the “other” choice is picked. Set its `relevant` for `select_one`: `${<question>} = 'other'`; for `select_multiple`: `selected(${<question>}, 'other')`. A `select_multiple` value lists every ticked code, so `=` would only match when “other” is the sole answer. See the `select_one_other` and `select_multiple_other` examples.

## Exclusive answers (`exclusive` column)

Applies to: `select_multiple`. For an answer that rules out all others (“Keine Angabe”, “Nichts davon”, “Weiß nicht”), add the `exclusive` column to the `choices` sheet and set it to `yes` on that choice. Leave it empty on every other row. Don't write a `count-selected()` constraint for this: LimeSurvey only gets it as a validation equation.

## Random answer order (`parameters: randomize=true`)

Applies to: `select_one`, `select_multiple` (also from a file). Write `randomize=true` in the `parameters` column to shuffle the options, e.g. to avoid primacy effects. LimeSurvey shuffles them too, and keeps a `select_multiple`'s `exclusive` answers at their position (LimeSurvey 6.17 or later); ODK and Kobo shuffle every option. Don't add a `seed`: LimeSurvey has none and drops it.

## Long lists from a file (`select_*_from_file`)

Type pattern: `^select_(one|multiple)_from_file (?P<filename>[^ ]+\.csv)$` — e.g. `select_one_from_file iso_3166_1.csv`. Use for long, standardised controlled vocabularies instead of hundreds of inline choices. Registered vocabularies:

| File | Vocabulary | Standard |
|---|---|---|
| `iso_3166_1.csv` | ISO 3166-1 country codes (alpha-2) | ISO 3166-1 |

## Skip logic & validation (`relevant`, `constraint`)

Written in the XLSForm XPath subset. `${name}` references another answer; `.` (in `constraint`) refers to this answer; `selected(${q}, 'code')` tests a choice. `constraint_message` holds the plain-text error.

To limit how many answers a `select_multiple` takes, write `count-selected(.) <= 3` (or `>= 1`, or both joined with `and`) as its `constraint`: LimeSurvey gets `max_answers` / `min_answers`. `count-selected(${q}) > 1` in a `relevant` counts the ticked answers of an earlier question.

**Only these functions are supported** (anything else is rejected):

`and`, `or`, `not`, `if`, `coalesce`, `selected`, `contains`, `starts-with`, `ends-with`, `regex`, `string`, `number`, `concat`, `substring`, `string-length`, `normalize-space`, `count`, `count-selected`, `sum`, `round`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `div`, `mod`, `today`, `now`

## Appearances (`appearance` column)

| `appearance` | Meaning | Valid on |
|---|---|---|
| `autocomplete` | Dropdown with search (autocomplete) | `select_one`, `select_one_from_file` |
| `field-list` | Field list group | `begin_group` |
| `horizontal` | Horizontal choices (buttons) | `select_one` |
| `horizontal-compact` | Horizontal choices, compact (buttons) | `select_one` |
| `label` | Matrix header row | `begin_group`, `select_one` |
| `likert` | Likert appearance hint | `select_one` |
| `list-nolabel` | Matrix body row | `select_one` |
| `minimal` | Dropdown / minimal display | `select_one`, `select_one_from_file` |
| `multiline` | Multi-line text | `text` |
| `table-list` | Table list (matrix) | `begin_group` |

## Multi-language

Add per-language columns `label::<lang>`, `hint::<lang>`, etc., where `<lang>` is an IETF BCP-47 tag (`de`, `en`, `fr-BE`), bare or in parentheses after a name (`label::Deutsch (de)`). Set `default_language` on the `settings` sheet the same way.

LimeSurvey has a fixed set of language codes. A regional tag it lacks falls back to its language with a warning (`fr-BE` → `fr`); a language it lacks entirely (e.g. `eo`), or two tags that land on one code (`fr` and `fr-BE`), fails the LimeSurvey conversion. DDI keeps every tag as written.

## `settings` sheet

| Key | Required |
|---|---|
| `form_title` | yes |
| `form_id` | yes |
| `default_language` | no |
| `version` | no |
| `instance_name` | no |

**Conventional magic rows:**

- type=note + name=welcome → Body text from label promoted to survey-level intro. Convention only; opt-in via tool config.
- type=note + name=end → End-of-survey thank-you. LS-only.

**LimeSurvey survey settings** (optional `limesurvey_<setting>` columns; ODK and Kobo ignore them, LimeSurvey gets an `S` row each; anything else is dropped with a `setting-invalid` warning):

| Column | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `limesurvey_allowprev` | `Y` `N` | a Previous button |
| `limesurvey_allowsave` | `Y` `N` | respondents can save and resume later |
| `limesurvey_showprogress` | `Y` `N` | a progress bar |
| `limesurvey_showxquestions` | `Y` `N` | 'There are N questions in this survey' (counts hidden and filtered questions too) |
| `limesurvey_showgroupinfo` | `B` `N` `D` `X` | group name and description: B both, N name, D description, X neither |
| `limesurvey_showqnumcode` | `B` `N` `C` `X` | question number and code: B both, N number, C code, X neither |
| `limesurvey_shownoanswer` | `Y` `N` | a 'No answer' option on optional questions (formtransform writes N unless the hideNoAnswer option is false) |
| `limesurvey_showwelcome` | `Y` `N` | the welcome page |
| `limesurvey_questionindex` | `0` `1` `2` | a question index: 0 none, 1 incremental, 2 full |
| `limesurvey_nokeyboard` | `Y` `N` | an on-screen keyboard |
| `limesurvey_printanswers` | `Y` `N` | respondents can print their answers |
| `limesurvey_autoredirect` | `Y` `N` | redirect to the end URL when the survey is completed |
| `limesurvey_navigationdelay` | `^[0-9]+$` | seconds before the navigation buttons are enabled |
| `limesurvey_anonymized` | `Y` `N` | anonymized responses |
| `limesurvey_datestamp` | `Y` `N` | store the date and time of each response |
| `limesurvey_ipaddr` | `Y` `N` | store the respondent's IP address |
| `limesurvey_ipanonymize` | `Y` `N` | anonymize the stored IP address |
| `limesurvey_refurl` | `Y` `N` | store the referrer URL |
| `limesurvey_savetimings` | `Y` `N` | store the time spent on each page and question |
| `limesurvey_template` | `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` | the theme's name (it must be installed in LimeSurvey) |

Not settable, derived from the form: `language` (`default_language` (else the first language)), `additional_languages` (the form's other languages (`label::<lang>` columns)), `format` (`style: pages` gives G (a page per group), anything else A (all in one)).
